newsitem.title: USA: Northeast to seek costs from ratepayers.
newsitem.headline: Northeast to seek costs from ratepayers.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Wednesday it might seek up to $340 million from Connecticut ratepayers to recover its $990 million in nuclear outage-related losses.

Northeast Chairman and Chief Executive Bernard Fox told state regulators at a hearing that the utility was likely to ask customers to pay no more than half of its $600 million in replacement power costs through 1998.
Fox also said Northeast would spend about $100 million for capacity reliability projects, of which it might seek about $40 million from ratepayers.

Fox "speculated on a range for the amount that we might seek to recover," Northeast spokeswoman Myra Humphries told Reuters. She said nothing was certain until the utility's three Millstone nuclear power plants are back on line.

The Millstone plants in Waterford, Conn., have been closed for safety reasons since March 1996. Northeast has said it intends to have them ready for restart by early 1998, pending approval by federal regulators.
Of the $990 million, the utility plans to spend about $300 million on operating and maintenance for the nuclear outages, Humphries said.
"We would seek none of that ($300 million from ratepayers)," Humphries said.

She said that left roughly $600 million for projected replacement power costs through 1998. "It would absolutely be less than half of the $600 million (that Northeast would seek from ratepayers), and probably significantly less than half, but there's no way to really categorize (it)," she said.
"There's no way we would determine how much of that we would seek until the plants are back on line."
"But because everybody wants a number, we're trying to quantify it," she said. (--Hartford bureau 860-727-0224)
